sb_across_the_rift.description:
Two other ramps cross this Rift besides mine, and I haven't had a warden near either since the cliffhawks started. That's four months. I'll say that plainly, because it's my failure. I had the people, and I kept them on the ramp I could see, which is exactly how you lose the other two.

Walk the west ramp, then the east, and tell me what's on them. The Rift is wider than it looks from up here, and it's always quieter than it should be, and that's how people get into trouble down there.

Look for hawks, cats, and anything that has no business on a ramp. Bones are normal, because we've been losing animals off these crossings since the Waystation went up. Fresh bones aren't. If you find fresh ones, come straight back.
sb_across_the_rift.accept_text: Take a lantern even at noon. The Rift floor is in shadow most of the day.
sb_across_the_rift.turn_in_text:
Both ramps are passable? Then the Waystation can breathe, and I can finally put wardens back where they should have been.

This is for you, and think of me kindly when you cross.

sb_blind_hunter.description:
There's a hunter in the western galleries I'd have called a story half a year ago. He's been blind for years, and everyone in that hill knows it, and he doesn't miss.

I've lost two friends to him, both scouts like me, good and quiet, and quiet is exactly the wrong qualification against a man who's listening. The second one carried nothing, no pack and no mail, and he was taken clean through the dark at a range Oggra's best archer couldn't make with his eyes open. Something about that gallery carries sound to him, and he's spent years learning its shape.

Kill his Razorfen Handlers, because a blind hunter being walked to you is a different problem from one who has to find you. He's in the west gallery, past Aggem's pen. Don't stand still.
sb_blind_hunter.accept_text: Move when he's shooting, stand still when he's listening. You'll learn the rhythm quickly.
sb_blind_hunter.turn_in_text:
The hunter's dead, and I'll write to the families properly now.

Here's something for you, with my thanks.

sb_cut_the_fuse.description:
Now for the one that's really urgent. I've been sitting on it for three days trying to be sure. Bael'dun's explosives experts have run a charge-line to the east gate, and I've followed it with the glass as far as the rock. It goes up the cliff.

If that line is fired, it brings the cliff down on the Waystation road, and that road is how everything north of here gets anywhere. I don't think it's a threat, and that's what's kept me up. I think it's a precaution, laid by somebody careful, for a day they're expecting.

I want the Dwarf Explosives Experts gone and the charges in my hands before that day comes. They wear the little red hats. Take their charges, and don't drop them. That sounds obvious, but it isn't, if you've ever met a dwarf.
sb_cut_the_fuse.accept_text: Cut the line in more than one place if you can. One cut can be spliced by morning.
sb_cut_the_fuse.turn_in_text:
You brought the charges back, all of them intact.

I'm truly impressed. Don't tell anyone I said so, because I've got a reputation that took years.

sb_down_the_stair.description:
Now for the stair. It doesn't go down, and you need that in your head before you're standing on it. It goes round. It's a spiral, and I've measured it twice and got two different answers, which I find personally insulting, because measuring well is the one thing nobody's ever disputed about me.

The Hive Drones and Hive Skulkers patrol the outer ring. Thin them so I can get in there with chalk, because an unchalked spiral is how a person ends up walking the same ring for hours convinced he's descending.

Keep to the right-hand wall, and it'll bring you to the middle whether you like it or not. The Broodspiral is south-east of here, under the Sinkhole Crater.
sb_down_the_stair.accept_text: Chalk a mark every twenty paces so I can check your count.
sb_down_the_stair.turn_in_text:
You came back with all your fingers, too.

I'm adding that to the map. It's a data point.

sb_eyes_on_the_gate.description:
I'm Zhuul, and I came down to the Waystation for a hot meal and a dry night, and I'm back up to the Keep at dawn.

I've been lying in the grass outside Bael'dun Keep, north-west of here, for two months with a spyglass and a bad attitude, and one of those is professional. The dwarves have turned Bael'dun into a proper fortress, with riflemen on the walls and patrols working the yard on a rotation I could set a clock by. That isn't a mining camp protecting itself, mon. It's a garrison.

I need the gate scouted and the Bael'dun Riflemen thinned before one of them spots me. Walk up to the gate, look, and come back. I'd go myself, but I'd leave a trail through that grass you could follow from the wall.
sb_eyes_on_the_gate.accept_text: Come back by a different route than you went in. They'll have seen the grass move.
sb_eyes_on_the_gate.turn_in_text:
That's good, very good.

The gate's guarded, but not as well as they think, and that gap is the whole of my job.

sb_geodes_for_the_warden.description:
Here's something my wardens worked out on their own, and I'm still proud of them for it. The Gravel Skitterers on the Rift floor carry geodes in their shells, like pockets. They don't eat them or use them, they just have them. And the crystals inside hum before a rockfall.

They don't hum during it, they hum before. One of my people heard her bag singing and stepped left, and the ramp she'd been standing on went into the canyon about four seconds later. A string of them along that ramp is worth a warden's life. They're unhappily worth a skitterer's life too, and I'd rather say so than not.

Bring me the geodes. If the skitterer objects, don't take it personally.
sb_geodes_for_the_warden.accept_text: Hold one to your ear on the way back. If it hums, get off the ramp first and ask questions after.
sb_geodes_for_the_warden.turn_in_text:
Listen to that, they really hum!

That's one fewer funeral this season, and I know exactly whose.

sb_giants_knucklebones.description:
The old plain has more than bones in it. It's got something that wears them. The Bone-Dust Wraiths are dust-grey, and they drift between the ribs out there carrying knuckles the size of anvils on their shoulders, like a man carrying a sack.

They keep them close, the way a miser keeps coins. I've watched one put a knuckle down and pick it straight back up again. I want those knuckles. I won't tell you why, and I'd rather be short about it than lie to you, but I'll pay you enough that you won't need the reason.

Take what you can off them, and don't let them take anything of yours. Watch their hands.
sb_giants_knucklebones.turn_in_text:
Look at the polish on that, it's beautiful.

This is for you. I'll be busy carving for a while, and I'd rather be left to it.

sb_golem_cores.description:
The dwarves have built stone golems to haul rock. They're grey and square, and they thump up and down those terraces all day and all night, obeying orders and never tiring. That last part is what I'd like explained.

I've watched one of those things work a full day and then keep working, and nothing on this plain does that. A kodo stops. A dwarf stops, badly and late, but he stops. So something is running them, and it isn't food or water.

Crack one open. There's a core in the chest, and it glows. Bring me shards of it. And don't spend too long thinking about what they run on, because I did that for a week and it only got me a short temper.
sb_golem_cores.accept_text: Wrap the shards in cloth. They glow through a sack, and that draws attention.
sb_golem_cores.turn_in_text:
They're running on nothing, or on something doing a very good impression of nothing.

I'll send word north.

sb_grubbs_ledger.description:
Foreman Grubb Deepdelver has run this pit since before the Keep was built, and he keeps a ledger. He counts the ore, the workers and the accidents. Notice that he counts the accidents, because a man who doesn't care doesn't write them down. I've watched him stop a line, at a cost, to get a figure right.

That's why I want those pages. A man who counts that carefully knows exactly what he's counting toward, and the number's in there even if the reason isn't. The overseers carry the day's sheets up to him in their satchels.

Take the pages off them, and deal with Grubb himself if he comes up for air. He's stubborn, and he's paid by the cubic yard, so you know how he'll fight.
sb_grubbs_ledger.accept_text: Bring me the newest page first. The old ones I can guess.
sb_grubbs_ledger.turn_in_text:
Look at these numbers. They've been digging for something specific. I don't know what it is, but they know where it is, and that's worse.

Take your reward. I'll write this up tonight.

sb_hawks_over_the_rift.description:
I'm Brakka Stonehoof. Stand back from the edge while we talk, not for the drop, but for the updraft.

The Rift is a day's walk of broken canyon between Camp Taurajo and everything south of it, and there's no way round. People try every season, and the Waystation goes out and finds what's left of them. I keep the ramp that crosses it, and that's the whole job. The Rift Cliffhawks have started nesting in the walls. They don't mind the caravans at all. A wagon could go past a nest all day. They mind the people on the ramp, whom they see, quite reasonably from where they sit, as dinner.

Thin them along the walls, and don't fall in. The Rift isn't forgiving about that.
sb_hawks_over_the_rift.accept_text: Keep one hand on the rope rail when they dive. They're trying to knock you off, not kill you.
sb_hawks_over_the_rift.turn_in_text:
It's quieter already, and I can hear the wagons again.

This is yours. It's the least the Waystation owes you.

sb_hyenas_in_the_bones.description:
I'm Rurk, a bone-hunter. Before you make the face, because everybody does, it's a trade, and it feeds people.

I hunt giant bones, the kind that stick up out of the Field of Giants like the ribs of a ship. They've been there longer than anyone has a story for. The Giantbone Hyenas have made the work harder, and in a clever way, which I resent more than the danger. They've learned that a man with his arms full of bones can't swing a spear. So they wait. They let you load up, and then they come in a pack, and you choose between your morning's work and your arm.

Drive them off the bones. I'll make a much better living if I'm not being chased across a plain I'm meant to be working.
sb_hyenas_in_the_bones.accept_text: Don't carry anything while you fight them. That's exactly what they're waiting for.
sb_hyenas_in_the_bones.turn_in_text:
Do you know what I'll hear out there tomorrow? Nothing at all.

You'd be surprised how good that sounds after a season of it.

sb_into_the_kraul.description:
Every thorn on that ridge grows out of the same root. I've said that for four winters and been laughed at for most of them. The root is the Kraul, the quilboar hill-warren south of my post, with a mouth of bramble and a throat of boars. Everything you've cleared off that ridge came out of it: the skinners, the hounds, Garn, and Durga's hedge.

I've watched that hill for four winters, and it's never looked as busy as it does now. Something in the Kraul's being made ready.

The gate is south of my post, under the thorns. Kill the Razorfen Spearhides at the door and the Razorfen Beast Trainers just inside. Be quick, and keep your back to the wall. The wall is mostly thorn, so mind it.
sb_into_the_kraul.accept_text: Burn the bramble at the mouth as you go in. It'll make the way out a lot easier.
sb_into_the_kraul.turn_in_text:
You've dealt with the spears and the whips, and you've still got all your fingers, so you'll do.

This is for you. We're going deeper.

sb_ironvein.description:
Sergeant Ironvein runs the east wall of Bael'dun Keep, north-west of here, and I've come to think he is the east wall. He drills the riflemen, and he walks the mastiffs himself at least twice a week, when the other sergeants only do it on paper. And he hammers every plan flat before it leaves the yard. I've watched three officers walk out of that gate with an idea and come back without it.

Most garrisons rot from the inside, because nobody's willing to say no to a bad plan. If Ironvein falls, the east gate falls.

He's up on the walls among the Bael'dun Sergeants, so listen for the hammer. Dwarves fight better in lines than loose, so break the line first and take them one at a time after.
sb_ironvein.accept_text: Break his hammer if you get the chance. The yard will hear it stop.
sb_ironvein.turn_in_text:
Ironvein's dead, and the east gate's lost its anchor.

This will hurt them for a season, and they won't work out why for most of it.

sb_mastiffs_at_the_gate.description:
The dwarves keep mastiffs, big, loud, mean and loyal, and I've no complaint about any of those on their own. They've started ranging out past the walls. One of them found my last lean-to, and it was a good lean-to that had held for six weeks.

That means the perimeter they're watching is bigger than the one I planned round, and a spy who's planned round the wrong perimeter has a short future. So I'd like the Keep Mastiffs gone, and while we're at it, I'd like what they've been guarding. The sergeants walk them, and the sergeants carry dispatches. That's a dwarf's idea of security, the orders right next to the teeth.

Bring me the dispatches. I don't read dwarvish, but I know a man who does, and he owes me a lot more than this.
sb_mastiffs_at_the_gate.turn_in_text:
These dispatches are orders for the east gate.

The dwarves are digging in, and that isn't the same as digging.

sb_razorbeak.description:
This one isn't a cull, and I want the difference on the record after what I've asked of you. There's an alpha out there called Razorbeak, and she's been raiding other nests for the eggs.

She breaks them, one by one. She doesn't eat them, and she doesn't take them anywhere. I followed her for two days to be certain, because I didn't believe it the first time. The grounds are going quiet because of her, which is worse than thinner, because it means nothing's hatching. I hate waste, and I hate it a lot more when it's deliberate. I've decided she is.

The Nest-Mother Raptors are protecting what's left of the clutches, and they'll come at you first, and they're right to. Then deal with her. She's fast, so don't stand still.
sb_razorbeak.accept_text: In the Raptor Grounds, among the nests. Kill the nest-mothers first.
sb_razorbeak.turn_in_text:
Razorbeak's gone, and the nests will recover.

Here's something for your trouble, with my thanks.

sb_razorflank.description:
At the top of the Kraul there's a platform of bones and a hut of thorn and tusk, and Charlga Razorflank sits in it. She's heard the pens fall and the speakers die. Nothing you've done in that hill has been a secret from her.

The hill's heart is hers. The thorn on that ridge grows because she wants it to, and Oggra has four winters of measurements to prove it. Kill her, and the thorns wither by spring. Oggra's wanted to say that to somebody who could do it since her first winter out there, and she asked me to say it for her.

The Razorfen Totemics round her mend each other as fast as you cut them, so cutting them is a losing game. Go for her first if you can. The thorns won't forgive you for it, but they'll stop.
sb_razorflank.turn_in_text:
Charlga's dead at last. The Kraul will take a generation to recover, if it ever does, and that ridge will breathe for the first time since anybody in Taurajo was born.

This is yours, with all the thanks Oggra has in her, and mine.

sb_screen_the_queen.turn_in_text:
The screen's down and you're alive, and you were the part I was worried about.

I'll chalk the throne room onto my map on the next trip. Take this, with my thanks and my apologies in advance.

sb_seed_and_thorn.description:
I'm Ashhoof, and I scout for the camp, and these days mostly for Oggra. The thorns on that ridge aren't wild. Take that seriously, because everyone Oggra reports to treats it as a figure of speech, and it's a plain fact.

The geomancers inside the Kraul plant them, one barbed pod at a time, pushed into the ground by hand. Every pod is a little more hill the quilboar own. That's how a thornwatch loses a ridge. It isn't a battle. It's a pod a day for ten years, and one morning your post is a hundred paces inside somebody else's country.

Bring me pods for Oggra's notes, because a pod on a table is evidence. Kill the Razorfen Geomancers who plant them. Handle the pods by the stem, because they open if you squeeze them, and they don't close again.
sb_seed_and_thorn.accept_text: Go into Razorfen Kraul. Its mouth is south of Oggra's thornwatch post, where the thorn closes over the road. The geomancers work the ground just inside, on their knees.
sb_seed_and_thorn.turn_in_text:
The thorn's spreading faster than I'd feared.

And now Oggra can prove it to somebody who outranks her, which is what she's needed all along.

sb_skinners_trophy_cords.description:
I'm Oggra, and I keep the thornwatch on the Razorfen approach, and I've done it four winters, which is three more than anybody before me.

The Razormane skinners have started wandering south of the Ridge. They braid trophy cords out of whatever they kill. That's old practice, and I wouldn't trouble you over a quilboar keeping to his habits. What's new is what's on them. A skinner knots in the names of who he took, and I've got rangers who went south of that Ridge and never came back. I've never been able to write to a single one of their families with anything better than a guess.

Bring me the cords. Look for the small bell on them, because that's how the skinners recognise each other.
sb_skinners_trophy_cords.turn_in_text:
These are names, and a great many of them are dead rangers.

I'll write to their families properly, with something true in it.

sb_skinwalker_garn.description:
There's a story on Blackthorn Ridge, and I'll tell it the way I heard it. A Razormane called Garn skins what he kills and wears what he takes. I heard it from three people in four winters and filed it with the rest of the thornwatch folklore, along with the singing well and the two-headed boar.

Then a ranger came back with half his coat missing. It wasn't torn. It had been cut away clean, from a man who got out alive and couldn't tell me afterwards when it had happened. So it isn't folklore. It's a working method, and I've been slow about it.

Garn works with the Razormane Seers. They're his eyes and they're how he gets close, so kill them first, and then him. Watch his hands. He can wear a face the way you'd wear a hat.
sb_skinwalker_garn.accept_text: Keep your coat buttoned and your back covered. He takes from behind.
sb_skinwalker_garn.turn_in_text:
Garn's dead, and the Ridge feels lighter.

Keep this close, and don't let anybody peel your coat.

sb_skyshriek.description:
At the heart of the spires there's a hollow where the wind never stops.

A matron has taken it, and named herself after it. Skyshriek commands the windcallers and sets the dust devils loose, and now I've seen where she does it from, I understand how. She isn't calling the wind. She's sitting in the only place out here that already has some. I want her gone before the next storm, because a storm plus that hollow plus a harpy who knows what to do with both is something I'd rather not find out about.

The hollow's at the arch, near the east edge. Look for the biggest nest. She'll scream, and that isn't the attack. It's what comes before it.
sb_skyshriek.accept_text: When she screams, get behind something solid. The wind comes a heartbeat after.
sb_skyshriek.turn_in_text:
The wind's dropped. Listen to that.

It's the quietest the spires have been in years.

sb_something_below.description:
You there, I'm only up at the Waystation for rope, so let's be quick.

I'm Fizzwick Boltcog. I found the Sinkhole Crater last spring, and I've been digging in it ever since, which my former partner calls an obsession and I call a schedule. I found a stair at the bottom, cut and dressed and going down. I found a great deal of glittering rock, which I won't be discussing. And three days ago I found what my notes call a series of unfortunate bites.

The Sinkhole Burrowers came up through the floor of my own dig, which is the one direction I hadn't budgeted for, and they're still coming. They're little brown things with lots of legs, and extremely rude. Thin them, and I'll get back to work. And no, you can't see what I've found. It's nothing personal.
sb_something_below.accept_text: Don't touch the glittering rock. It isn't yours, and I'll know.
sb_something_below.turn_in_text:
Marvellous, that's done!

I've sorted three crates already. Don't look at them.

sb_teeth_in_the_canyon.description:
The sabertooths came down out of the high rock three weeks ago, and that isn't normal. They've got everything they need up there. I've watched them for six years, and they've never once had a reason to come to the ramp.

A caravan of kodo-haulers lost two animals and a driver, and every survivor told me the same thing, separately: something bigger than a sabertooth was watching from the ledges. They called it Dustmaw. My mother used that name to get me off the ramp at dusk, and I'd put it away with the rest of the stories forty years ago.

Kill the Rift Sabertooths first, because they're what's killing people. Dustmaw, if he shows himself, is the reason they came down at all.
sb_teeth_in_the_canyon.accept_text: Walk the ramp in daylight. The cats are bolder after dusk, and so is whatever brought them.
sb_teeth_in_the_canyon.turn_in_text:
Dustmaw's really dead?

I'll hang a fang over the gate, and I'll take it down again the first time a child asks me whether the story's true. You've earned a bigger share than that.

sb_the_beast_pit.description:
I'm Tull, and I keep the camp's kodo, and I've been counting the ones that don't come back. From the pens, a narrow neck runs north-west, and it's sealed with wards, stones set into the rock and held by Ward-Keepers who do nothing else.

That's the Beast Pit. There's a thing in it called Agathelos, and they've been feeding it on stolen kodo for years. Break the ward-stones and the ward falls, and then it isn't in any more. I've thought hard about leaving it sealed. But the seal holds because quilboar maintain it, and the day they open that neck themselves will be a day they choose, not us.

Kill the Razorfen Ward-Keepers, break the stones, then go in. Agathelos is a beast, not a boar, so don't mistake one for the other.
sb_the_beast_pit.turn_in_text:
Agathelos is dead, and the pit's open to the sun.

I hope that rattles Charlga, and I think it will.

sb_the_boarhound_pack.accept_text: Listen for the whistle. If you hear it, the pack's about to turn on whoever's closest.

sb_the_bramble_court.description:
South of my post, the thorns grow thick and the quilboar grow thicker, and that's where this ends. A Bristleback matriarch called Durga has taken the Razorfen approach for her court.

She's grown her bramble-guard round her like a hedge, and I mean that word. It isn't a bodyguard, it's a planted boundary with quilboar in it, and it's been getting wider all winter. I've measured it four times, and it's a hundred paces further out than when I took the post. The Razorfen approach is closing, and when it closes, everything south of the Ridge belongs to her.

Kill the Razorfen Bramble-Guards, then the Thornhide Boars, then the queen. Don't change that order to be clever, and stay on dry ground.
sb_the_bramble_court.accept_text: Burn the hedge as you go if the wind's right. It's the only thing that stops it growing.
sb_the_bramble_court.turn_in_text:
The Bramble Court is finished, and the approach is open.

You've done more for the Barrens than a battalion, and a battalion would have been given a banner for it. These are yours.

sb_the_matriarchs_last_walk.description:
There's a herd-mother out on the Field of Giants walking in circles. She's been at it a season, on the same ground, goring anything that comes near her, and the herders call her Old Mother Longhorn.

She isn't mad, and I need that said before I ask you. She lost a calf somewhere out there in the bones, and she's been looking for it ever since, and the circle is the search. The Aged Kodo of her herd walk it with her, and they won't let you near her while they're standing. I won't do it myself. I think it would be bad luck for a man in my trade, and you can think what you like of that.

I pay well, though, and I'd ask you to be quick about it. She's been grieving long enough.
sb_the_matriarchs_last_walk.accept_text: If you find the calf's bones out there, leave them where they lie. She'd want them left.
sb_the_matriarchs_last_walk.turn_in_text:
It's done, then. I hope it was quiet.

This is yours. Say a word for her on the road, if you've got one in you.

sb_the_overseers.description:
Behind every dwarf with a pick there's a dwarf with a whip, and behind him there's one with a wrench. The miners dig, the overseers keep the miners moving, and the engineers keep the overseers supplied. I've spent a month watching it, and it's a good chain. Nobody idles, and nobody waits for anything.

A chain breaks in the middle. We've thinned the miners, and they replaced them inside a fortnight without losing an hour. Take out the middle, and the top has nobody to give orders to and the bottom has nobody giving them.

The Modan Overseers wear red sashes, and the Dwarf Engineers carry wrenches the size of your arm. Kill both, in any order you like.
sb_the_overseers.accept_text: Leave the miners if you can help it. It's the sashes and the wrenches I want gone.
sb_the_overseers.turn_in_text:
The pit's gone quiet, with whole terraces standing idle. That's good work.

There's one more thing to chase down there, but take this first.

sb_the_pens_below.description:
At the centre of the Kraul are the Boar Pens, a corral ring with stalls on every side, and Overlord Ramtusk stands in the middle of it. He's been fattening boars for a war for ten years.

Let that number land. That isn't a raiding herd, because you don't need ten years for raids, you need a season and a bad winter. Ten years is somebody with a date in mind, who's had it since before Oggra took her post. I want the pens broken before anybody opens them.

The ring has three gaps. Hold the south one, and they'll come to you through it, because the open version of this fight is a hundred boars and no corners. Kill the Thornback Sows as they come, and keep them off your back while you're looking at him.
sb_the_pens_below.accept_text: Bring rope if you can. A gate you can tie shut is a gate you can stop worrying about.
sb_the_pens_below.turn_in_text:
The Overlord's dead, and the pens are empty.

Oggra will sleep tonight, for the first time in four winters.

sb_the_pit_at_bael_modan.description:
I'm Tarrik, so lie down before you come up to the rim, because the glare's behind us and you'll be a shape on the skyline.

The dwarves at Bael Modan have been digging for years. That isn't news, and it isn't a war, because people dig. I've watched this pit since before it had terraces, and for most of that time I wrote it up as mining and went home. Here's what changed. I count heads. Every month there are more miners and the hole is deeper, and the two numbers are climbing together in a way mining doesn't. A mine slows down when you hit hard rock or water or the end of a seam. This one has never once slowed.

So I want fewer Dwarf Miners, and I want to know what they're digging toward. Keep an eye on the bottom of that pit while you're down there.
sb_the_pit_at_bael_modan.accept_text: Look for anything at the bottom that isn't rock. That's what I really want to know about.
sb_the_pit_at_bael_modan.turn_in_text:
And the pit's still going. They didn't even stop to look at their own dead.

That's the part that worries me, not the digging.

sb_the_raptor_cull.accept_text: Count the nests as you pass them. I'll want to know how many there are for next season.

sb_the_tenders.description:
Past the outer ring, the tunnel widens into a brood chamber. The things that tend it are called brood tenders, and I've been told they're quite gentle.

I want to be careful about where that came from, because it matters. I was told it by somebody who isn't coming back. So I'm passing it on with that attached, rather than letting it sit in your head as a fact, which is more than anyone did for me when I started this dig.

The Broodkeeper sits at the head of the chamber, behind a pair of resin pillars. You'll see them from the entry, because they're the only straight lines down there. Kill the Brood Tenders first, then the Broodkeeper. And stay out of the green. The green isn't for you. The Broodspiral is south-east of here.
sb_the_tenders.accept_text: Kill the tenders quickly. They're gentle, as I said, but they won't stay that way while you're in the room.
sb_the_tenders.turn_in_text:
The Broodkeeper's dead, and the second ring's open.

I'm very proud of you, and also deeply afraid, and I'd like both noted.

sb_the_vine_bridge.description:
West of the first fork there's a rope-and-vine bridge over a drop, and on the platform at the far end lives Roogug. He's been ordering that hill's warriors about since before Oggra was a ranger.

Oggra's officers say that because he's off the main road, he's safe to leave alone, and strictly that's true. Nothing he does threatens the ridge directly. She'd rather he weren't left alone, and so would I, because a quilboar who's given orders for thirty years and never once been tested is one everybody in there still listens to.

The bridge is narrow, so don't fight on it, or you'll lose your party one at a time. Wait on the platform, and Roogug will come to you, with his Razorfen Defenders. He's all muscle and no plan, so use that.
sb_the_vine_bridge.accept_text: Test each plank before you put your weight on it. The quilboar don't repair anything.
sb_the_vine_bridge.turn_in_text:
Roogug's down, and the bridge is quiet for the first time in my life.

Here's something for you, with my thanks.

sb_thrumbone.description:
There's something out there older than the bones. Think about that, because I've had three years with it. Those ribs have been on that plain since before anybody wrote anything down about this continent, and there's a thing walking among them that was there first.

The wraiths gather round it. It walks a slow circle through the ribs, and when it does, the ground hums. I've felt that hum through my boots from a mile off. I call it Thrumbone. I've never seen it. I've had every chance, and I've turned away from all of them.

I want it gone. Kill the Bone-Dust Wraiths first. Then, if you feel the ground start to sing, that's him. I'd run, and that's exactly why you're the one being paid. The Field of Giants is south of here.
sb_thrumbone.accept_text: Put your hand flat on the ground now and then. You'll feel him before you hear him.
sb_thrumbone.turn_in_text:
They tell me the ground out there's gone quiet, for the first time in years. Thank you.

These are yours. They belong to the plain now, and so do you, whether or not that's what you wanted.

sb_two_speakers.description:
I'm Rohan, and I keep the camp's war drums, and while Oggra's out on the ridge, I send people into the Kraul for her.

North of the fork, the Kraul splits round the Thorn Court, and a chieftain sits at either end of it. Aggem Thorncurse holds the west, and he calls the boar-spirits. Death Speaker Jargba holds the east, and he speaks for the dead, and he takes what they tell him very seriously. Oggra's spent four winters working out which of them runs this hill, and the answer's neither, which is why both have to go.

Take them in whatever order you like. Aggem's guards are beast-trainers with boars, and Jargba's are Death's Head, with hexes. Don't fight both courts at once, and don't let either of them finish a sentence.
sb_two_speakers.accept_text: Bring someone who can break a hex. Death's Head work lingers after the caster falls.
sb_two_speakers.turn_in_text:
You got both of them!

I'd call the hill's spirit broken, but Oggra's been out there long enough to know better, and she'd tell me so. This is yours, with my respect.

sb_vexa.description:
At the bottom of the crater, past the guards and past everything, there's a queen called Vexa. The Sinkhole isn't just occupied by her, it's hers, the way a house is somebody's, and the Broodspiral below is her nursery.

I want the stair. That's been my whole aim since last spring, and I won't pretend it's changed. But I'd also like the nursery intact, because a thing like that going down takes the ring with it, and nothing grows back in a crater. I can't have either while she's alive, and there's no deal to be made with her.

Go down and find the nest at the centre. She's big and angry, and she won't stop. Neither should you, and that's the actual tactic. The Sinkhole Crater is south-east of here.
sb_vexa.accept_text: Mind the nursery walls when she charges. I'd like them standing afterwards.
sb_vexa.turn_in_text:
The queen's dead, and the stair's open. I'm going to need a bigger shovel.

Here's your reward, with my deepest thanks and a cheque I'll never in my life cash.

sb_voices_in_the_spires.description:
The wind sings through those spires. It did long before the harpies came, and it'll do it after, because that's the rock. The windcallers sing with it, and where they sing, the dust gets up and turns on you. I've watched a dust devil change direction against the wind to reach a traveller, which is the most unnatural thing I've seen in this country.

So I want the Hoodoo Dust Devils broken, and I want the crystals the windcallers carry. The crystals sing too, quietly, in a pocket, whether or not a harpy's holding them, and I'd rather they did it for me than for the harpies.

They're about the size of your thumb. Take them, and come back before you start humming along. Everyone does, after about an hour.
sb_voices_in_the_spires.turn_in_text:
They're singing in my pocket, and it isn't unpleasant.

Here's something for you. And please stop humming.

sb_windspire_harpies.description:
I'm Alamir, and I've come in off the Hoodoo Spires to restock arrows, so I'll be going straight back out.

The spires in the north-east are full of wind and voices, and I can't tell you which is which any more. Windspire Harpies nest in the hollows up there and shriek down at anything that passes underneath. It isn't a warning, and it isn't about territory. I've watched them do it to an empty road. I've hunted them for a season, my arrows are running low, and my patience went some while before that.

Kill them in the hollows on the east side. And don't stand under the spires, because they drop things. I don't think they do it on purpose, but that doesn't improve the outcome.
sb_windspire_harpies.accept_text: Shoot them on the way down, not when they're perched. They're clumsy in the air.
sb_windspire_harpies.turn_in_text: It's quiet up there at last. You could almost hear yourself think.

tau_can_kodo_go_down.description: I sent somebody up to the Lift once already and got back the word that there were trees on it. I've had three years to make peace with that, and about four days to make peace with the rest. There's a way down now, and what I need to know is whether a kodo can take it, because a road a kodo can't walk is only a footpath with ambitions. Walk the whole thing, from where the timber stops at the head of the descent down to where the road forks on the valley floor. I'm asking about the slope, the footing and whether there's water in the first two days, and you'll only know that by putting your own feet on it.
tau_can_kodo_go_down.accept_text: Count the switchbacks as you go. A kodo turns wide, and every one of them matters.
tau_can_kodo_go_down.turn_in_text:
You said passable, not good.

That's the first honest answer anyone's brought me about that country, and I've been asking for three years.

tau_road_south.description: I'm not asking you to fix it. I'm asking you to walk up and look at it, because I've asked four people and got four different mountains back. Go to where the Lift stood. The winch house is still bolted to the rock, and the cable runs out thirty feet and straight into granite. Past that, there's a line in the ground where the red dust stops and the leaf mould starts, as sharp as a knife cut. Stand on it, and tell me what's on the other side.
tau_road_south.accept_text: Take a sprig of whatever grows on the far side, if you can. I'd like to hold it.
tau_road_south.turn_in_text:
You're standing there telling me there are trees? I drove that road for twenty years, and there was sky and a very long drop and nothing else on it. Now there are trees growing where the drop used to be.

Sit down a moment. I need a moment with that.
